**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>April 2010</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for January 2010** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for January 2010 world copper supply and demand in its April 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to the preliminary ICSG data, including revisions to data previously presented, the refined copper market balance for January 2010, both actual and seasonally adjusted for usage and production, indicated a market surplus of around 120,000 metric tonnes (t). This compares with a surplus of around 160,000 t (actual and adjusted) in January 2009: A year-on year increase in world consumption was more than offset by an increase in production. 

In January 2010, world usage is estimated to have increased by 11% (150,000 t) compared with that in the same month of 2009. Chinese apparent usage<sup>*****</sup> grew by 11%, but when compared with that in December 2009 it decreased by 13%.  Other contributors to higher consumption in January 2010 were Japan, South Korea, the EU and the Gulf countries, with estimated usage in the United States remaining flat.  World usage recovered in all regions with the exception of North America where it remained unchanged. 

World mine production grew by 2.5% (30,000 t) in January 2010 compared with that in January 2009: Concentrate production grew by 2.8% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 1.2%. Production in the two leading copper mine producers, Chile and Peru, decreased by an aggregated 2.2%. Africa and Oceania were the main contributors to growth, with an aggregated increase of 28%. Mine production capacity utilization was 77%, around the same level as January 2009 but below that in December 2009. 

In January 2010, world refined production increased by 7% (110,000 t) compared with the same month of 2009: Primary production increased by 2.2%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 43%. Note that production of secondary refined copper in January 2009 was at a low level owing to a tight scrap market, and that primary refined copper production was reduced by recently announced production cuts, both in response to the rapid decline in price.  Refined production increased by 65% in Africa, 11% in Asia, and 10% in Europe, but decreased in the Americas and Oceania by 4% and 9%, respectively. Refined production capacity utilization increased to 79.5% compared with 76% in January 2009. 

The average LME cash price for March 2010 was US$7,462.83 per tonne, up from the February 2009 average of US$6,848.18 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of March were US$7,830 and US$6,242 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,243.39 per tonne. As of the end of March 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 757,758 t, an increase of 70,067 t from stocks held at the end

of December 2009.
